[[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] [[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] [[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q1346974]] Wikidata name: Sesshō and Kampaku [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:15, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Types of regent in Imperial Japan}} {{About|the regent of the Emperor|the regent of a shōgun|Shikken}} {{DISPLAYTITLE:''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku''}} [[File:Japan Sessyo Flag.svg|thumb|right|250px|Imperial Standard of the Regent]] In {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}, {{Nihongo||摂政|'''Sesshō'''}} was a {{ill|Regent|en|Regent|WD=Q477406|lt=Regent}} who was named to act on behalf of either a child {{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|WD=Q208233|lt=emperor}} before his {{ill|coming of age|en|coming of age|WD=Q681737|lt=coming of age}}, or an {{ill|Empress of Japan|en|Empress of Japan|WD=Q595038|lt=empress regnant}}. The {{Nihongo||関白|'''Kampaku'''}} was theoretically a sort of chief advisor for the Emperor, but was in practice the title of both [[:en:First Minister|first secretary]] and {{ill|Regent|en|Regent|WD=Q477406|lt=Regent}} who assisted an adult Emperor. The duties of the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' were to convey to the Emperor the policies formulated by the {{nihongo3|[[Minister of the Left]]|左大臣|1=Minister of the Left|Sadaijin}} and other senior officials of the {{nihongo3|[[Council of State]]|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|[[Daijō-kan]]}}, and to convey the Emperor's decisions to them. As regents of the Emperor, the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' sometimes made decisions on behalf of the Emperor, but their positions were not defined by law and they had no specific political authority. The two titles were collectively known as {{Nihongo||摂関|'''sekkan'''}}, and the families that exclusively held the titles were called {{transl|ja|sekkan-ke}} ({{transl|ja|sekkan}} family). During the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}} (794–1185), from the middle of the 9th century, the [[Fujiwara clan]] began to marry off their daughters to the Emperor and assume the positions of ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', thereby excluding other clans from the political centre and increasing their political power. From the 10th century, the Fujiwara clan monopolized the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', and at the end of the 10th century, around the time of {{ill|Fujiwara no Michinaga|en|Fujiwara no Michinaga|WD=Q433133|lt=Fujiwara no Michinaga}} and {{ill|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|en|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|WD=Q1370620|lt=Fujiwara no Yorimichi}}, the power of the Fujiwara clan reached its zenith. In the mid-11th century, [[:en:Emperor Go-Sanjo|Emperor Go-Sanjo]] ran his own government, and the next Emperor, {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|en|Emperor Shirakawa|WD=Q60949|lt=Shirakawa}}, abdicated to become {{ill|Cloistered Emperor|en|Cloistered Emperor|WD=Q3053200|lt=Cloistered Emperor}}, beginning the {{ill|Cloistered rule|en|Cloistered rule|WD=Q865416|lt=Cloistered rule}}. From then on, the cloistered rule of Cloistered Emperor took root, and the de facto Fujiwara regime, which used the positions of ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', was over, and the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' lost their real political power and became mere names.{{cite web|url=https://www.juku.st/info/entry/1349|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220511095734/https://www.juku.st/info/entry/1349|script-title=ja:【藤原道長はなぜ躍進？】摂関政治をわかりやすく説明する方法|language=ja|publisher=Tomonokai|date=19 July 2015|archive-date=11 May 2022|access-date=11 March 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://news.yahoo.co.jp/expert/articles/d404674899919ce02e297e8f3a5117f8807b3341|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240312002713/https://news.yahoo.co.jp/expert/articles/d404674899919ce02e297e8f3a5117f8807b3341|script-title=ja:摂関政治で最盛期を築き上げた藤原氏とは、いかなる由緒を持つ氏族なのか|language=ja|publisher=Yahoo News|date=4 January 2024|archive-date=12 March 2024|access-date=12 March 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E6%91%82%E9%96%A2%E6%94%BF%E6%B2%BB-87197|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231129224719/https://kotobank.jp/word/%E6%91%82%E9%96%A2%E6%94%BF%E6%B2%BB-87197|script-title=ja:摂関政治|language=ja|publisher=Kotobank|date=|archive-date=29 November 2023|access-date=13 March 2024}} During the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|WD=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period}} (1185–1333), when the warrior class seized power and the {{ill|Kamakura shogunate|en|Kamakura shogunate|WD=Q736839|lt=Kamakura shogunate}} was established, the Fujiwara were divided into {{nihongo|{{ill|Five regent houses|en|Five regent houses|WD=Q1067142|lt=Five regent houses}}|五摂家|Go-sekke}}: the {{ill|Konoe family|en|Konoe family|WD=Q1781840|lt=Konoe}}, {{ill|Kujō family|en|Kujō family|WD=Q1791350|lt=Kujō}}, {{ill|Nijō family|en|Nijō family|WD=Q3065387|lt=Nijō}}, {{ill|Ichijō family|en|Ichijō family|WD=Q1535498|lt=Ichijo}}, and {{ill|Takatsukasa family|en|Takatsukasa family|WD=Q846799|lt=Takatsukasa}} families. From then on, these five families served as ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' on a rotating basis.{{cite web|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E4%BA%94%E6%91%82%E5%AE%B6-64979|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231208093025/https://kotobank.jp/word/%E4%BA%94%E6%91%82%E5%AE%B6-64979|script-title=ja:五摂家|language=ja|publisher=kotobank|date=|archive-date=8 December 2023|access-date=12 March 2024}} {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} was the first person in history to become a ''Kampaku'' who was not a noble by birth; his nephew {{ill|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|en|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|WD=Q967501|lt=Toyotomi Hidetsugu}} also became a ''Kampaku''. Hideyoshi obtained this title, the highest position in the aristocracy, by being adopted into the Konoe family and formally becoming an aristocrat. A retired {{transl|ja|Kampaku}} was called {{Nihongo||太閤|'''Taikō'''}}, which came to commonly refer to Toyotomi Hideyoshi.{{cite web|url=https://business.nikkei.com/atcl/opinion/16/122600033/010800002/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230905041529/https://business.nikkei.com/atcl/opinion/16/122600033/010800002/|script-title=ja:秀吉はなぜ征夷大将軍ではなく、関白を選んだか|language=ja|publisher=Nikkei Business|date=14 January 2017|archive-date=5 September 2023|access-date=29 February 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://dot.asahi.com/articles/-/202017?page=3|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240229075803/https://dot.asahi.com/articles/-/202017?page=3|script-title=ja:豊臣秀吉はなぜ「征夷大将軍」ではなく「関白」になったのか――秀吉をめぐる「三つのなぜ」|language=ja|publisher=[[The Asahi Shimbun]]|date=24 September 2023|archive-date=29 February 2024|access-date=29 February 2024}} Both {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} were styled as {{transl|ja|denka}} or {{nihongo||殿下|1=Highness|lt=Your Highness (Denka)|tenga}} in historical pronunciation; translated as "(Imperial) Highness", as were Imperial princes and princesses. ==History== In earlier times, only members of the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|en|Imperial House of Japan|WD=Q909452|lt=Imperial Family}} could be appointed {{transl|ja|sesshō}}. The {{transl|ja|[[Kojiki]]}} reports that {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ōjin}} was assisted by his mother, {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}}, but it is doubtful if it is a historical fact. The first historical {{transl|ja|sesshō}} was {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|en|Prince Shōtoku|WD=Q263972|lt=Prince Shōtoku}}, who assisted {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko}}. The [[Fujiwara clan]] was the primary holder of the {{transl|ja|kampaku}} and {{transl|ja|sesshō}} titles. More precisely, those titles were held by the [[:en:Hokke (Fujiwara)|Fujiwara Hokke]] (northern Fujiwara family) and its descendants, to which {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshifusa|en|Fujiwara no Yoshifusa|WD=Q960841|lt=Fujiwara no Yoshifusa}} belonged. In 858, Fujiwara no Yoshifusa became {{transl|ja|sesshō}}. He was the first {{transl|ja|sesshō}} not to be a member of the Imperial house. In 887, {{ill|Fujiwara no Mototsune|en|Fujiwara no Mototsune|WD=Q1397196|lt=Fujiwara no Mototsune}}, the nephew and adopted son of Yoshifusa, was appointed to the newly created office of {{transl|ja|kampaku}}. In the 12th century, there were {{ill|Five regent houses|en|Five regent houses|WD=Q1067142|lt=five families}} among the descendants of Yorimichi called {{transl|ja|sekke}}: the {{ill|Konoe family|en|Konoe family|WD=Q1781840|lt=Konoe family}}, {{ill|Kujō family|en|Kujō family|WD=Q1791350|lt=Kujō family}}, {{ill|Ichijō family|en|Ichijō family|WD=Q1535498|lt=Ichijō family}}, {{ill|Takatsukasa family|en|Takatsukasa family|WD=Q846799|lt=Takatsukasa family}} and {{ill|Nijō family|en|Nijō family|WD=Q3065387|lt=Nijō family}}. Both the Konoe and Kujō families were descendants of {{ill|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|en|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|WD=Q1370620|lt=Fujiwara no Yorimichi}}, through {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadamichi|en|Fujiwara no Tadamichi|WD=Q1354407|lt=Fujiwara no Tadamichi}}. The other three families were derived from either the Konoe or Kujō families. Until the [[Meiji Restoration]] of 1868, those five families held those title exclusively with the two exceptions of {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} and his nephew {{ill|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|en|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|WD=Q967501|lt=Toyotomi Hidetsugu}}. The offices and titles of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} were abolished by the declaration of the Imperial Restoration in 1868 during the Meiji Restoration in order to reorganize the government structure. The office and title of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} was stipulated under the former {{ill|Imperial Household Law|en|Imperial Household Law|WD=Q1324733|lt=Imperial Household Law}} in 1889 and also under the new Imperial Household Law in 1948. Under these laws, the officeholder of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} is restricted to a member of the Imperial family. [[:en:Crown Prince|Crown Prince]] {{ill|Hirohito|en|Hirohito|WD=Q34479|lt=Hirohito}}, before becoming Emperor Shōwa, was {{transl|ja|sesshō}} from 1921 to 1926 for the mentally disabled {{ill|Emperor Taishō|en|Emperor Taishō|WD=Q157052|lt=Emperor Taishō}}. He was called {{Nihongo3|"the Prince-Regent"|摂政宮|sesshō-no-miya}}. The area of Taikō in Nagoya is named after the title, although it refers to Toyotomi Hideyoshi. The main street is Taikō-dōri, which is served by the subway {{ill|Taiko-dori Station|en|Taiko-dori Station|WD=Q850809|lt=Taiko-dori Station}}. ==List== The following is a list of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} in the order of succession.{{cite web| url= http://nekhet.ddo.jp/ruler/japan/sekkan.html| script-title= ja:摂政・関白| access-date= 2007-09-20| language= ja| author= ネケト| location= {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=JP}}| url-status= dead| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20040827224301/http://nekhet.ddo.jp/ruler/japan/sekkan.html| archive-date= 2004-08-27}} The list is not exhaustive: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" |- ! scope="col" | Portrait ! scope="col" width="200px" | Name ! width="100px" | Regent title ! scope="col" width="100px"| Tenure ! scope="col" | Monarch |- |[[File:Umayado Miko.jpg|200x200px]] |'''{{ill|Prince Shōtoku|en|Prince Shōtoku|WD=Q263972|lt=Prince Shōtoku}}'''

[[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] [[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] [[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] {{Short description|Types of regent in Imperial Japan}} {{About|the regent of the Emperor|the regent of a shōgun|Shikken}} {{DISPLAYTITLE:''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku''}} [[File:Japan Sessyo Flag.svg|thumb|right|250px|Imperial Standard of the Regent]] In {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}, {{Nihongo||摂政|'''Sesshō'''}} was a {{ill|Regent|en|Regent|WD=Q477406|lt=Regent}} who was named to act on behalf of either a child {{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|WD=Q208233|lt=emperor}} before his {{ill|coming of age|en|coming of age|WD=Q681737|lt=coming of age}}, or an {{ill|Empress of Japan|en|Empress of Japan|WD=Q595038|lt=empress regnant}}. The {{Nihongo||関白|'''Kampaku'''}} was theoretically a sort of chief advisor for the Emperor, but was in practice the title of both [[:en:First Minister|first secretary]] and {{ill|Regent|en|Regent|WD=Q477406|lt=Regent}} who assisted an adult Emperor. The duties of the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' were to convey to the Emperor the policies formulated by the {{nihongo3|[[Minister of the Left]]|左大臣|1=Minister of the Left|Sadaijin}} and other senior officials of the {{nihongo3|[[Council of State]]|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|[[Daijō-kan]]}}, and to convey the Emperor's decisions to them. As regents of the Emperor, the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' sometimes made decisions on behalf of the Emperor, but their positions were not defined by law and they had no specific political authority. The two titles were collectively known as {{Nihongo||摂関|'''sekkan'''}}, and the families that exclusively held the titles were called {{transl|ja|sekkan-ke}} ({{transl|ja|sekkan}} family). During the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}} (794–1185), from the middle of the 9th century, the [[Fujiwara clan]] began to marry off their daughters to the Emperor and assume the positions of ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', thereby excluding other clans from the political centre and increasing their political power. From the 10th century, the Fujiwara clan monopolized the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', and at the end of the 10th century, around the time of {{ill|Fujiwara no Michinaga|en|Fujiwara no Michinaga|WD=Q433133|lt=Fujiwara no Michinaga}} and {{ill|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|en|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|WD=Q1370620|lt=Fujiwara no Yorimichi}}, the power of the Fujiwara clan reached its zenith. In the mid-11th century, [[:en:Emperor Go-Sanjo|Emperor Go-Sanjo]] ran his own government, and the next Emperor, {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|en|Emperor Shirakawa|WD=Q60949|lt=Shirakawa}}, abdicated to become {{ill|Cloistered Emperor|en|Cloistered Emperor|WD=Q3053200|lt=Cloistered Emperor}}, beginning the {{ill|Cloistered rule|en|Cloistered rule|WD=Q865416|lt=Cloistered rule}}. From then on, the cloistered rule of Cloistered Emperor took root, and the de facto Fujiwara regime, which used the positions of ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', was over, and the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' lost their real political power and became mere names.{{cite web|url=https://www.juku.st/info/entry/1349|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220511095734/https://www.juku.st/info/entry/1349|script-title=ja:【藤原道長はなぜ躍進？】摂関政治をわかりやすく説明する方法|language=ja|publisher=Tomonokai|date=19 July 2015|archive-date=11 May 2022|access-date=11 March 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://news.yahoo.co.jp/expert/articles/d404674899919ce02e297e8f3a5117f8807b3341|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240312002713/https://news.yahoo.co.jp/expert/articles/d404674899919ce02e297e8f3a5117f8807b3341|script-title=ja:摂関政治で最盛期を築き上げた藤原氏とは、いかなる由緒を持つ氏族なのか|language=ja|publisher=Yahoo News|date=4 January 2024|archive-date=12 March 2024|access-date=12 March 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E6%91%82%E9%96%A2%E6%94%BF%E6%B2%BB-87197|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231129224719/https://kotobank.jp/word/%E6%91%82%E9%96%A2%E6%94%BF%E6%B2%BB-87197|script-title=ja:摂関政治|language=ja|publisher=Kotobank|date=|archive-date=29 November 2023|access-date=13 March 2024}} During the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|WD=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period}} (1185–1333), when the warrior class seized power and the {{ill|Kamakura shogunate|en|Kamakura shogunate|WD=Q736839|lt=Kamakura shogunate}} was established, the Fujiwara were divided into {{nihongo|{{ill|Five regent houses|en|Five regent houses|WD=Q1067142|lt=Five regent houses}}|五摂家|Go-sekke}}: the {{ill|Konoe family|en|Konoe family|WD=Q1781840|lt=Konoe}}, {{ill|Kujō family|en|Kujō family|WD=Q1791350|lt=Kujō}}, {{ill|Nijō family|en|Nijō family|WD=Q3065387|lt=Nijō}}, {{ill|Ichijō family|en|Ichijō family|WD=Q1535498|lt=Ichijo}}, and {{ill|Takatsukasa family|en|Takatsukasa family|WD=Q846799|lt=Takatsukasa}} families. From then on, these five families served as ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' on a rotating basis.{{cite web|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E4%BA%94%E6%91%82%E5%AE%B6-64979|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231208093025/https://kotobank.jp/word/%E4%BA%94%E6%91%82%E5%AE%B6-64979|script-title=ja:五摂家|language=ja|publisher=kotobank|date=|archive-date=8 December 2023|access-date=12 March 2024}} {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} was the first person in history to become a ''Kampaku'' who was not a noble by birth; his nephew {{ill|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|en|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|WD=Q967501|lt=Toyotomi Hidetsugu}} also became a ''Kampaku''. Hideyoshi obtained this title, the highest position in the aristocracy, by being adopted into the Konoe family and formally becoming an aristocrat. A retired {{transl|ja|Kampaku}} was called {{Nihongo||太閤|'''Taikō'''}}, which came to commonly refer to Toyotomi Hideyoshi.{{cite web|url=https://business.nikkei.com/atcl/opinion/16/122600033/010800002/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230905041529/https://business.nikkei.com/atcl/opinion/16/122600033/010800002/|script-title=ja:秀吉はなぜ征夷大将軍ではなく、関白を選んだか|language=ja|publisher=Nikkei Business|date=14 January 2017|archive-date=5 September 2023|access-date=29 February 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://dot.asahi.com/articles/-/202017?page=3|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240229075803/https://dot.asahi.com/articles/-/202017?page=3|script-title=ja:豊臣秀吉はなぜ「征夷大将軍」ではなく「関白」になったのか――秀吉をめぐる「三つのなぜ」|language=ja|publisher=[[The Asahi Shimbun]]|date=24 September 2023|archive-date=29 February 2024|access-date=29 February 2024}} Both {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} were styled as {{transl|ja|denka}} or {{nihongo||殿下|1=Highness|lt=Your Highness (Denka)|tenga}} in historical pronunciation; translated as "(Imperial) Highness", as were Imperial princes and princesses. ==History== In earlier times, only members of the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|en|Imperial House of Japan|WD=Q909452|lt=Imperial Family}} could be appointed {{transl|ja|sesshō}}. The {{transl|ja|[[Kojiki]]}} reports that {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ōjin}} was assisted by his mother, {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}}, but it is doubtful if it is a historical fact. The first historical {{transl|ja|sesshō}} was {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|en|Prince Shōtoku|WD=Q263972|lt=Prince Shōtoku}}, who assisted {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko}}. The [[Fujiwara clan]] was the primary holder of the {{transl|ja|kampaku}} and {{transl|ja|sesshō}} titles. More precisely, those titles were held by the [[:en:Hokke (Fujiwara)|Fujiwara Hokke]] (northern Fujiwara family) and its descendants, to which {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshifusa|en|Fujiwara no Yoshifusa|WD=Q960841|lt=Fujiwara no Yoshifusa}} belonged. In 858, Fujiwara no Yoshifusa became {{transl|ja|sesshō}}. He was the first {{transl|ja|sesshō}} not to be a member of the Imperial house. In 887, {{ill|Fujiwara no Mototsune|en|Fujiwara no Mototsune|WD=Q1397196|lt=Fujiwara no Mototsune}}, the nephew and adopted son of Yoshifusa, was appointed to the newly created office of {{transl|ja|kampaku}}. In the 12th century, there were {{ill|Five regent houses|en|Five regent houses|WD=Q1067142|lt=five families}} among the descendants of Yorimichi called {{transl|ja|sekke}}: the {{ill|Konoe family|en|Konoe family|WD=Q1781840|lt=Konoe family}}, {{ill|Kujō family|en|Kujō family|WD=Q1791350|lt=Kujō family}}, {{ill|Ichijō family|en|Ichijō family|WD=Q1535498|lt=Ichijō family}}, {{ill|Takatsukasa family|en|Takatsukasa family|WD=Q846799|lt=Takatsukasa family}} and {{ill|Nijō family|en|Nijō family|WD=Q3065387|lt=Nijō family}}. Both the Konoe and Kujō families were descendants of {{ill|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|en|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|WD=Q1370620|lt=Fujiwara no Yorimichi}}, through {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadamichi|en|Fujiwara no Tadamichi|WD=Q1354407|lt=Fujiwara no Tadamichi}}. The other three families were derived from either the Konoe or Kujō families. Until the [[Meiji Restoration]] of 1868, those five families held those title exclusively with the two exceptions of {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} and his nephew {{ill|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|en|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|WD=Q967501|lt=Toyotomi Hidetsugu}}. The offices and titles of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} were abolished by the declaration of the Imperial Restoration in 1868 during the Meiji Restoration in order to reorganize the government structure. The office and title of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} was stipulated under the former {{ill|Imperial Household Law|en|Imperial Household Law|WD=Q1324733|lt=Imperial Household Law}} in 1889 and also under the new Imperial Household Law in 1948. Under these laws, the officeholder of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} is restricted to a member of the Imperial family. [[:en:Crown Prince|Crown Prince]] {{ill|Hirohito|en|Hirohito|WD=Q34479|lt=Hirohito}}, before becoming Emperor Shōwa, was {{transl|ja|sesshō}} from 1921 to 1926 for the mentally disabled {{ill|Emperor Taishō|en|Emperor Taishō|WD=Q157052|lt=Emperor Taishō}}. He was called {{Nihongo3|"the Prince-Regent"|摂政宮|sesshō-no-miya}}. The area of Taikō in Nagoya is named after the title, although it refers to Toyotomi Hideyoshi. The main street is Taikō-dōri, which is served by the subway {{ill|Taiko-dori Station|en|Taiko-dori Station|WD=Q850809|lt=Taiko-dori Station}}. ==List== The following is a list of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} in the order of succession.{{cite web| url= http://nekhet.ddo.jp/ruler/japan/sekkan.html| script-title= ja:摂政・関白| access-date= 2007-09-20| language= ja| author= ネケト| location= {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=JP}}| url-status= dead| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20040827224301/http://nekhet.ddo.jp/ruler/japan/sekkan.html| archive-date= 2004-08-27}} The list is not exhaustive: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" |- ! scope="col" | Portrait ! scope="col" width="200px" | Name ! width="100px" | Regent title ! scope="col" width="100px"| Tenure ! scope="col" | Monarch |- |[[File:Umayado Miko.jpg|200x200px]] |'''{{ill|Prince Shōtoku|en|Prince Shōtoku|WD=Q263972|lt=Prince Shōtoku}}'''

[[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] [[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] [[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] {{Short description|Types of regent in Imperial Japan}} {{About|the regent of the Emperor|the regent of a shōgun|Shikken}} {{DISPLAYTITLE:''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku''}} [[File:Japan Sessyo Flag.svg|thumb|right|250px|Imperial Standard of the Regent]] In {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}, {{Nihongo||摂政|'''Sesshō'''}} was a {{ill|Regent|en|Regent|WD=Q477406|lt=Regent}} who was named to act on behalf of either a child {{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|WD=Q208233|lt=emperor}} before his {{ill|coming of age|en|coming of age|WD=Q681737|lt=coming of age}}, or an {{ill|Empress of Japan|en|Empress of Japan|WD=Q595038|lt=empress regnant}}. The {{Nihongo||関白|'''Kampaku'''}} was theoretically a sort of chief advisor for the Emperor, but was in practice the title of both [[:en:First Minister|first secretary]] and {{ill|Regent|en|Regent|WD=Q477406|lt=Regent}} who assisted an adult Emperor. The duties of the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' were to convey to the Emperor the policies formulated by the {{nihongo3|[[Minister of the Left]]|左大臣|1=Minister of the Left|Sadaijin}} and other senior officials of the {{nihongo3|[[Council of State]]|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|[[Daijō-kan]]}}, and to convey the Emperor's decisions to them. As regents of the Emperor, the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' sometimes made decisions on behalf of the Emperor, but their positions were not defined by law and they had no specific political authority. The two titles were collectively known as {{Nihongo||摂関|'''sekkan'''}}, and the families that exclusively held the titles were called {{transl|ja|sekkan-ke}} ({{transl|ja|sekkan}} family). During the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}} (794–1185), from the middle of the 9th century, the [[Fujiwara clan]] began to marry off their daughters to the Emperor and assume the positions of ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', thereby excluding other clans from the political centre and increasing their political power. From the 10th century, the Fujiwara clan monopolized the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', and at the end of the 10th century, around the time of {{ill|Fujiwara no Michinaga|en|Fujiwara no Michinaga|WD=Q433133|lt=Fujiwara no Michinaga}} and {{ill|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|en|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|WD=Q1370620|lt=Fujiwara no Yorimichi}}, the power of the Fujiwara clan reached its zenith. In the mid-11th century, [[:en:Emperor Go-Sanjo|Emperor Go-Sanjo]] ran his own government, and the next Emperor, {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|en|Emperor Shirakawa|WD=Q60949|lt=Shirakawa}}, abdicated to become {{ill|Cloistered Emperor|en|Cloistered Emperor|WD=Q3053200|lt=Cloistered Emperor}}, beginning the {{ill|Cloistered rule|en|Cloistered rule|WD=Q865416|lt=Cloistered rule}}. From then on, the cloistered rule of Cloistered Emperor took root, and the de facto Fujiwara regime, which used the positions of ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', was over, and the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' lost their real political power and became mere names.{{cite web|url=https://www.juku.st/info/entry/1349|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220511095734/https://www.juku.st/info/entry/1349|script-title=ja:【藤原道長はなぜ躍進？】摂関政治をわかりやすく説明する方法|language=ja|publisher=Tomonokai|date=19 July 2015|archive-date=11 May 2022|access-date=11 March 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://news.yahoo.co.jp/expert/articles/d404674899919ce02e297e8f3a5117f8807b3341|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240312002713/https://news.yahoo.co.jp/expert/articles/d404674899919ce02e297e8f3a5117f8807b3341|script-title=ja:摂関政治で最盛期を築き上げた藤原氏とは、いかなる由緒を持つ氏族なのか|language=ja|publisher=Yahoo News|date=4 January 2024|archive-date=12 March 2024|access-date=12 March 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E6%91%82%E9%96%A2%E6%94%BF%E6%B2%BB-87197|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231129224719/https://kotobank.jp/word/%E6%91%82%E9%96%A2%E6%94%BF%E6%B2%BB-87197|script-title=ja:摂関政治|language=ja|publisher=Kotobank|date=|archive-date=29 November 2023|access-date=13 March 2024}} During the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|WD=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period}} (1185–1333), when the warrior class seized power and the {{ill|Kamakura shogunate|en|Kamakura shogunate|WD=Q736839|lt=Kamakura shogunate}} was established, the Fujiwara were divided into {{nihongo|{{ill|Five regent houses|en|Five regent houses|WD=Q1067142|lt=Five regent houses}}|五摂家|Go-sekke}}: the {{ill|Konoe family|en|Konoe family|WD=Q1781840|lt=Konoe}}, {{ill|Kujō family|en|Kujō family|WD=Q1791350|lt=Kujō}}, {{ill|Nijō family|en|Nijō family|WD=Q3065387|lt=Nijō}}, {{ill|Ichijō family|en|Ichijō family|WD=Q1535498|lt=Ichijo}}, and {{ill|Takatsukasa family|en|Takatsukasa family|WD=Q846799|lt=Takatsukasa}} families. From then on, these five families served as ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' on a rotating basis.{{cite web|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E4%BA%94%E6%91%82%E5%AE%B6-64979|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231208093025/https://kotobank.jp/word/%E4%BA%94%E6%91%82%E5%AE%B6-64979|script-title=ja:五摂家|language=ja|publisher=kotobank|date=|archive-date=8 December 2023|access-date=12 March 2024}} {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} was the first person in history to become a ''Kampaku'' who was not a noble by birth; his nephew {{ill|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|en|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|WD=Q967501|lt=Toyotomi Hidetsugu}} also became a ''Kampaku''. Hideyoshi obtained this title, the highest position in the aristocracy, by being adopted into the Konoe family and formally becoming an aristocrat. A retired {{transl|ja|Kampaku}} was called {{Nihongo||太閤|'''Taikō'''}}, which came to commonly refer to Toyotomi Hideyoshi.{{cite web|url=https://business.nikkei.com/atcl/opinion/16/122600033/010800002/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230905041529/https://business.nikkei.com/atcl/opinion/16/122600033/010800002/|script-title=ja:秀吉はなぜ征夷大将軍ではなく、関白を選んだか|language=ja|publisher=Nikkei Business|date=14 January 2017|archive-date=5 September 2023|access-date=29 February 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://dot.asahi.com/articles/-/202017?page=3|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240229075803/https://dot.asahi.com/articles/-/202017?page=3|script-title=ja:豊臣秀吉はなぜ「征夷大将軍」ではなく「関白」になったのか――秀吉をめぐる「三つのなぜ」|language=ja|publisher=[[The Asahi Shimbun]]|date=24 September 2023|archive-date=29 February 2024|access-date=29 February 2024}} Both {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} were styled as {{transl|ja|denka}} or {{nihongo||殿下|1=Highness|lt=Your Highness (Denka)|tenga}} in historical pronunciation; translated as "(Imperial) Highness", as were Imperial princes and princesses. ==History== In earlier times, only members of the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|en|Imperial House of Japan|WD=Q909452|lt=Imperial Family}} could be appointed {{transl|ja|sesshō}}. The {{transl|ja|[[Kojiki]]}} reports that {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ōjin}} was assisted by his mother, {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}}, but it is doubtful if it is a historical fact. The first historical {{transl|ja|sesshō}} was {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|en|Prince Shōtoku|WD=Q263972|lt=Prince Shōtoku}}, who assisted {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko}}. The [[Fujiwara clan]] was the primary holder of the {{transl|ja|kampaku}} and {{transl|ja|sesshō}} titles. More precisely, those titles were held by the [[:en:Hokke (Fujiwara)|Fujiwara Hokke]] (northern Fujiwara family) and its descendants, to which {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshifusa|en|Fujiwara no Yoshifusa|WD=Q960841|lt=Fujiwara no Yoshifusa}} belonged. In 858, Fujiwara no Yoshifusa became {{transl|ja|sesshō}}. He was the first {{transl|ja|sesshō}} not to be a member of the Imperial house. In 887, {{ill|Fujiwara no Mototsune|en|Fujiwara no Mototsune|WD=Q1397196|lt=Fujiwara no Mototsune}}, the nephew and adopted son of Yoshifusa, was appointed to the newly created office of {{transl|ja|kampaku}}. In the 12th century, there were {{ill|Five regent houses|en|Five regent houses|WD=Q1067142|lt=five families}} among the descendants of Yorimichi called {{transl|ja|sekke}}: the {{ill|Konoe family|en|Konoe family|WD=Q1781840|lt=Konoe family}}, {{ill|Kujō family|en|Kujō family|WD=Q1791350|lt=Kujō family}}, {{ill|Ichijō family|en|Ichijō family|WD=Q1535498|lt=Ichijō family}}, {{ill|Takatsukasa family|en|Takatsukasa family|WD=Q846799|lt=Takatsukasa family}} and {{ill|Nijō family|en|Nijō family|WD=Q3065387|lt=Nijō family}}. Both the Konoe and Kujō families were descendants of {{ill|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|en|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|WD=Q1370620|lt=Fujiwara no Yorimichi}}, through {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadamichi|en|Fujiwara no Tadamichi|WD=Q1354407|lt=Fujiwara no Tadamichi}}. The other three families were derived from either the Konoe or Kujō families. Until the [[Meiji Restoration]] of 1868, those five families held those title exclusively with the two exceptions of {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} and his nephew {{ill|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|en|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|WD=Q967501|lt=Toyotomi Hidetsugu}}. The offices and titles of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} were abolished by the declaration of the Imperial Restoration in 1868 during the Meiji Restoration in order to reorganize the government structure. The office and title of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} was stipulated under the former {{ill|Imperial Household Law|en|Imperial Household Law|WD=Q1324733|lt=Imperial Household Law}} in 1889 and also under the new Imperial Household Law in 1948. Under these laws, the officeholder of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} is restricted to a member of the Imperial family. [[:en:Crown Prince|Crown Prince]] {{ill|Hirohito|en|Hirohito|WD=Q34479|lt=Hirohito}}, before becoming Emperor Shōwa, was {{transl|ja|sesshō}} from 1921 to 1926 for the mentally disabled {{ill|Emperor Taishō|en|Emperor Taishō|WD=Q157052|lt=Emperor Taishō}}. He was called {{Nihongo3|"the Prince-Regent"|摂政宮|sesshō-no-miya}}. The area of Taikō in Nagoya is named after the title, although it refers to Toyotomi Hideyoshi. The main street is Taikō-dōri, which is served by the subway {{ill|Taiko-dori Station|en|Taiko-dori Station|WD=Q850809|lt=Taiko-dori Station}}. ==List== The following is a list of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} in the order of succession.{{cite web| url= http://nekhet.ddo.jp/ruler/japan/sekkan.html| script-title= ja:摂政・関白| access-date= 2007-09-20| language= ja| author= ネケト| location= {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=JP}}| url-status= dead| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20040827224301/http://nekhet.ddo.jp/ruler/japan/sekkan.html| archive-date= 2004-08-27}} The list is not exhaustive: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" |- ! scope="col" | Portrait ! scope="col" width="200px" | Name ! width="100px" | Regent title ! scope="col" width="100px"| Tenure ! scope="col" | Monarch |- |[[File:Umayado Miko.jpg|200x200px]] |'''{{ill|Prince Shōtoku|en|Prince Shōtoku|WD=Q263972|lt=Prince Shōtoku}}'''

[[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] [[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] [[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] {{Short description|Types of regent in Imperial Japan}} {{About|the regent of the Emperor|the regent of a shōgun|Shikken}} {{DISPLAYTITLE:''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku''}} [[File:Japan Sessyo Flag.svg|thumb|right|250px|Imperial Standard of the Regent]] In {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}}, {{Nihongo||摂政|'''Sesshō'''}} was a {{ill|Regent|en|Regent|WD=Q477406|lt=Regent|1=Regent}} who was named to act on behalf of either a child {{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|WD=Q208233|lt=emperor|1=Emperor of Japan}} before his {{ill|coming of age|en|coming of age|WD=Q681737|lt=coming of age|1=Coming of age}}, or an {{ill|Empress of Japan|en|Empress of Japan|WD=Q595038|lt=empress regnant|1=Empress of Japan}}. The {{Nihongo||関白|'''Kampaku'''}} was theoretically a sort of chief advisor for the Emperor, but was in practice the title of both [[:en:First Minister|first secretary]] and {{ill|Regent|en|Regent|WD=Q477406|lt=Regent|1=Regent}} who assisted an adult Emperor. The duties of the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' were to convey to the Emperor the policies formulated by the {{nihongo3|[[Minister of the Left]]|左大臣|1=Minister of the Left|Sadaijin}} and other senior officials of the {{nihongo3|[[Council of State]]|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|[[Daijō-kan]]}}, and to convey the Emperor's decisions to them. As regents of the Emperor, the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' sometimes made decisions on behalf of the Emperor, but their positions were not defined by law and they had no specific political authority. The two titles were collectively known as {{Nihongo||摂関|'''sekkan'''}}, and the families that exclusively held the titles were called {{transl|ja|sekkan-ke}} ({{transl|ja|sekkan}} family). During the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}} (794–1185), from the middle of the 9th century, the [[Fujiwara clan]] began to marry off their daughters to the Emperor and assume the positions of ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', thereby excluding other clans from the political centre and increasing their political power. From the 10th century, the Fujiwara clan monopolized the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', and at the end of the 10th century, around the time of {{ill|Fujiwara no Michinaga|en|Fujiwara no Michinaga|WD=Q433133|lt=Fujiwara no Michinaga|1=Fujiwara no Michinaga}} and {{ill|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|en|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|WD=Q1370620|lt=Fujiwara no Yorimichi|1=Fujiwara no Yorimichi}}, the power of the Fujiwara clan reached its zenith. In the mid-11th century, [[:en:Emperor Go-Sanjo|Emperor Go-Sanjo]] ran his own government, and the next Emperor, {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|en|Emperor Shirakawa|WD=Q60949|lt=Shirakawa|1=Emperor Shirakawa}}, abdicated to become {{ill|Cloistered Emperor|en|Cloistered Emperor|WD=Q3053200|lt=Cloistered Emperor|1=Cloistered Emperor}}, beginning the {{ill|Cloistered rule|en|Cloistered rule|WD=Q865416|lt=Cloistered rule|1=Cloistered rule}}. From then on, the cloistered rule of Cloistered Emperor took root, and the de facto Fujiwara regime, which used the positions of ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', was over, and the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' lost their real political power and became mere names.{{cite web|url=https://www.juku.st/info/entry/1349|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220511095734/https://www.juku.st/info/entry/1349|script-title=ja:【藤原道長はなぜ躍進？】摂関政治をわかりやすく説明する方法|language=ja|publisher=Tomonokai|date=19 July 2015|archive-date=11 May 2022|access-date=11 March 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://news.yahoo.co.jp/expert/articles/d404674899919ce02e297e8f3a5117f8807b3341|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240312002713/https://news.yahoo.co.jp/expert/articles/d404674899919ce02e297e8f3a5117f8807b3341|script-title=ja:摂関政治で最盛期を築き上げた藤原氏とは、いかなる由緒を持つ氏族なのか|language=ja|publisher=Yahoo News|date=4 January 2024|archive-date=12 March 2024|access-date=12 March 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E6%91%82%E9%96%A2%E6%94%BF%E6%B2%BB-87197|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231129224719/https://kotobank.jp/word/%E6%91%82%E9%96%A2%E6%94%BF%E6%B2%BB-87197|script-title=ja:摂関政治|language=ja|publisher=Kotobank|date=|archive-date=29 November 2023|access-date=13 March 2024}} During the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|WD=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period|1=Kamakura period}} (1185–1333), when the warrior class seized power and the {{ill|Kamakura shogunate|en|Kamakura shogunate|WD=Q736839|lt=Kamakura shogunate|1=Kamakura shogunate}} was established, the Fujiwara were divided into {{nihongo|{{ill|Five regent houses|en|Five regent houses|WD=Q1067142|lt=Five regent houses|1=Five regent houses}}|五摂家|Go-sekke}}: the {{ill|Konoe family|en|Konoe family|WD=Q1781840|lt=Konoe|1=Konoe family}}, {{ill|Kujō family|en|Kujō family|WD=Q1791350|lt=Kujō|1=Kujō family}}, {{ill|Nijō family|en|Nijō family|WD=Q3065387|lt=Nijō|1=Nijō family}}, {{ill|Ichijō family|en|Ichijō family|WD=Q1535498|lt=Ichijo|1=Ichijō family}}, and {{ill|Takatsukasa family|en|Takatsukasa family|WD=Q846799|lt=Takatsukasa|1=Takatsukasa family}} families. From then on, these five families served as ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' on a rotating basis.{{cite web|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E4%BA%94%E6%91%82%E5%AE%B6-64979|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231208093025/https://kotobank.jp/word/%E4%BA%94%E6%91%82%E5%AE%B6-64979|script-title=ja:五摂家|language=ja|publisher=kotobank|date=|archive-date=8 December 2023|access-date=12 March 2024}} {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi|1=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} was the first person in history to become a ''Kampaku'' who was not a noble by birth; his nephew {{ill|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|en|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|WD=Q967501|lt=Toyotomi Hidetsugu|1=Toyotomi Hidetsugu}} also became a ''Kampaku''. Hideyoshi obtained this title, the highest position in the aristocracy, by being adopted into the Konoe family and formally becoming an aristocrat. A retired {{transl|ja|Kampaku}} was called {{Nihongo||太閤|'''Taikō'''}}, which came to commonly refer to Toyotomi Hideyoshi.{{cite web|url=https://business.nikkei.com/atcl/opinion/16/122600033/010800002/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230905041529/https://business.nikkei.com/atcl/opinion/16/122600033/010800002/|script-title=ja:秀吉はなぜ征夷大将軍ではなく、関白を選んだか|language=ja|publisher=Nikkei Business|date=14 January 2017|archive-date=5 September 2023|access-date=29 February 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://dot.asahi.com/articles/-/202017?page=3|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240229075803/https://dot.asahi.com/articles/-/202017?page=3|script-title=ja:豊臣秀吉はなぜ「征夷大将軍」ではなく「関白」になったのか――秀吉をめぐる「三つのなぜ」|language=ja|publisher=[[The Asahi Shimbun]]|date=24 September 2023|archive-date=29 February 2024|access-date=29 February 2024}} Both {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} were styled as {{transl|ja|denka}} or {{nihongo||殿下|1=Highness|lt=Your Highness (Denka)|tenga}} in historical pronunciation; translated as "(Imperial) Highness", as were Imperial princes and princesses. ==History== In earlier times, only members of the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|en|Imperial House of Japan|WD=Q909452|lt=Imperial Family|1=Imperial House of Japan}} could be appointed {{transl|ja|sesshō}}. The {{transl|ja|[[Kojiki]]}} reports that {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ōjin|1=Emperor Ōjin}} was assisted by his mother, {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū|1=Empress Jingū}}, but it is doubtful if it is a historical fact. The first historical {{transl|ja|sesshō}} was {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|en|Prince Shōtoku|WD=Q263972|lt=Prince Shōtoku|1=Prince Shōtoku}}, who assisted {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}}. The [[Fujiwara clan]] was the primary holder of the {{transl|ja|kampaku}} and {{transl|ja|sesshō}} titles. More precisely, those titles were held by the [[:en:Hokke (Fujiwara)|Fujiwara Hokke]] (northern Fujiwara family) and its descendants, to which {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshifusa|en|Fujiwara no Yoshifusa|WD=Q960841|lt=Fujiwara no Yoshifusa|1=Fujiwara no Yoshifusa}} belonged. In 858, Fujiwara no Yoshifusa became {{transl|ja|sesshō}}. He was the first {{transl|ja|sesshō}} not to be a member of the Imperial house. In 887, {{ill|Fujiwara no Mototsune|en|Fujiwara no Mototsune|WD=Q1397196|lt=Fujiwara no Mototsune|1=Fujiwara no Mototsune}}, the nephew and adopted son of Yoshifusa, was appointed to the newly created office of {{transl|ja|kampaku}}. In the 12th century, there were {{ill|Five regent houses|en|Five regent houses|WD=Q1067142|lt=five families|1=Five regent houses}} among the descendants of Yorimichi called {{transl|ja|sekke}}: the {{ill|Konoe family|en|Konoe family|WD=Q1781840|lt=Konoe family|1=Konoe family}}, {{ill|Kujō family|en|Kujō family|WD=Q1791350|lt=Kujō family|1=Kujō family}}, {{ill|Ichijō family|en|Ichijō family|WD=Q1535498|lt=Ichijō family|1=Ichijō family}}, {{ill|Takatsukasa family|en|Takatsukasa family|WD=Q846799|lt=Takatsukasa family|1=Takatsukasa family}} and {{ill|Nijō family|en|Nijō family|WD=Q3065387|lt=Nijō family|1=Nijō family}}. Both the Konoe and Kujō families were descendants of {{ill|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|en|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|WD=Q1370620|lt=Fujiwara no Yorimichi|1=Fujiwara no Yorimichi}}, through {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadamichi|en|Fujiwara no Tadamichi|WD=Q1354407|lt=Fujiwara no Tadamichi|1=Fujiwara no Tadamichi}}. The other three families were derived from either the Konoe or Kujō families. Until the [[Meiji Restoration]] of 1868, those five families held those title exclusively with the two exceptions of {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi|1=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} and his nephew {{ill|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|en|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|WD=Q967501|lt=Toyotomi Hidetsugu|1=Toyotomi Hidetsugu}}. The offices and titles of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} were abolished by the declaration of the Imperial Restoration in 1868 during the Meiji Restoration in order to reorganize the government structure. The office and title of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} was stipulated under the former {{ill|Imperial Household Law|en|Imperial Household Law|WD=Q1324733|lt=Imperial Household Law|1=Imperial Household Law}} in 1889 and also under the new Imperial Household Law in 1948. Under these laws, the officeholder of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} is restricted to a member of the Imperial family. [[:en:Crown Prince|Crown Prince]] {{ill|Hirohito|en|Hirohito|WD=Q34479|lt=Hirohito|1=Hirohito}}, before becoming Emperor Shōwa, was {{transl|ja|sesshō}} from 1921 to 1926 for the mentally disabled {{ill|Emperor Taishō|en|Emperor Taishō|WD=Q157052|lt=Emperor Taishō|1=Emperor Taishō}}. He was called {{Nihongo3|"the Prince-Regent"|摂政宮|sesshō-no-miya}}. The area of Taikō in Nagoya is named after the title, although it refers to Toyotomi Hideyoshi. The main street is Taikō-dōri, which is served by the subway {{ill|Taiko-dori Station|en|Taiko-dori Station|WD=Q850809|lt=Taiko-dori Station|1=Taiko-dori Station}}. ==List== The following is a list of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} in the order of succession.{{cite web| url= http://nekhet.ddo.jp/ruler/japan/sekkan.html| script-title= ja:摂政・関白| access-date= 2007-09-20| language= ja| author= ネケト| location= {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=JP|1=Japan}}| url-status= dead| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20040827224301/http://nekhet.ddo.jp/ruler/japan/sekkan.html| archive-date= 2004-08-27}} The list is not exhaustive: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" |- ! scope="col" | Portrait ! scope="col" width="200px" | Name ! width="100px" | Regent title ! scope="col" width="100px"| Tenure ! scope="col" | Monarch |- |[[File:Umayado Miko.jpg|200x200px]] |'''{{ill|Prince Shōtoku|en|Prince Shōtoku|WD=Q263972|lt=Prince Shōtoku|1=Prince Shōtoku}}'''

[[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] [[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] [[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] {{Short description|Types of regent in Imperial Japan}} {{About|the regent of the Emperor|the regent of a shōgun|Shikken}} {{DISPLAYTITLE:''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku''}} [[File:Japan Sessyo Flag.svg|thumb|right|250px|Imperial Standard of the Regent]] In {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}}, {{Nihongo||摂政|'''Sesshō'''}} was a {{ill|Regent|en|Regent|WD=Q477406|lt=Regent|1=Regent}} who was named to act on behalf of either a child {{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|WD=Q208233|lt=emperor|1=Emperor of Japan}} before his {{ill|coming of age|en|coming of age|WD=Q681737|lt=coming of age|1=Coming of age}}, or an {{ill|Empress of Japan|en|Empress of Japan|WD=Q595038|lt=empress regnant|1=Empress of Japan}}. The {{Nihongo||関白|'''Kampaku'''}} was theoretically a sort of chief advisor for the Emperor, but was in practice the title of both [[:en:First Minister|first secretary]] and {{ill|Regent|en|Regent|WD=Q477406|lt=Regent|1=Regent}} who assisted an adult Emperor. The duties of the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' were to convey to the Emperor the policies formulated by the {{nihongo3|[[Minister of the Left]]|左大臣|1=Minister of the Left|Sadaijin}} and other senior officials of the {{nihongo3|[[Council of State]]|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|[[Daijō-kan]]}}, and to convey the Emperor's decisions to them. As regents of the Emperor, the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' sometimes made decisions on behalf of the Emperor, but their positions were not defined by law and they had no specific political authority. The two titles were collectively known as {{Nihongo||摂関|'''sekkan'''}}, and the families that exclusively held the titles were called {{transl|ja|sekkan-ke}} ({{transl|ja|sekkan}} family). During the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}} (794–1185), from the middle of the 9th century, the [[Fujiwara clan]] began to marry off their daughters to the Emperor and assume the positions of ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', thereby excluding other clans from the political centre and increasing their political power. From the 10th century, the Fujiwara clan monopolized the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', and at the end of the 10th century, around the time of {{ill|Fujiwara no Michinaga|en|Fujiwara no Michinaga|WD=Q433133|lt=Fujiwara no Michinaga|1=Fujiwara no Michinaga}} and {{ill|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|en|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|WD=Q1370620|lt=Fujiwara no Yorimichi|1=Fujiwara no Yorimichi}}, the power of the Fujiwara clan reached its zenith. In the mid-11th century, [[:en:Emperor Go-Sanjo|Emperor Go-Sanjo]] ran his own government, and the next Emperor, {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|en|Emperor Shirakawa|WD=Q60949|lt=Shirakawa|1=Emperor Shirakawa}}, abdicated to become {{ill|Cloistered Emperor|en|Cloistered Emperor|WD=Q3053200|lt=Cloistered Emperor|1=Cloistered Emperor}}, beginning the {{ill|Cloistered rule|en|Cloistered rule|WD=Q865416|lt=Cloistered rule|1=Cloistered rule}}. From then on, the cloistered rule of Cloistered Emperor took root, and the de facto Fujiwara regime, which used the positions of ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', was over, and the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' lost their real political power and became mere names.{{cite web|url=https://www.juku.st/info/entry/1349|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220511095734/https://www.juku.st/info/entry/1349|script-title=ja:【藤原道長はなぜ躍進？】摂関政治をわかりやすく説明する方法|language=ja|publisher=Tomonokai|date=19 July 2015|archive-date=11 May 2022|access-date=11 March 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://news.yahoo.co.jp/expert/articles/d404674899919ce02e297e8f3a5117f8807b3341|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240312002713/https://news.yahoo.co.jp/expert/articles/d404674899919ce02e297e8f3a5117f8807b3341|script-title=ja:摂関政治で最盛期を築き上げた藤原氏とは、いかなる由緒を持つ氏族なのか|language=ja|publisher=Yahoo News|date=4 January 2024|archive-date=12 March 2024|access-date=12 March 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E6%91%82%E9%96%A2%E6%94%BF%E6%B2%BB-87197|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231129224719/https://kotobank.jp/word/%E6%91%82%E9%96%A2%E6%94%BF%E6%B2%BB-87197|script-title=ja:摂関政治|language=ja|publisher=Kotobank|date=|archive-date=29 November 2023|access-date=13 March 2024}} During the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|WD=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period|1=Kamakura period}} (1185–1333), when the warrior class seized power and the {{ill|Kamakura shogunate|en|Kamakura shogunate|WD=Q736839|lt=Kamakura shogunate|1=Kamakura shogunate}} was established, the Fujiwara were divided into {{nihongo|{{ill|Five regent houses|en|Five regent houses|WD=Q1067142|lt=Five regent houses|1=Five regent houses}}|五摂家|Go-sekke}}: the {{ill|Konoe family|en|Konoe family|WD=Q1781840|lt=Konoe|1=Konoe family}}, {{ill|Kujō family|en|Kujō family|WD=Q1791350|lt=Kujō|1=Kujō family}}, {{ill|Nijō family|en|Nijō family|WD=Q3065387|lt=Nijō|1=Nijō family}}, {{ill|Ichijō family|en|Ichijō family|WD=Q1535498|lt=Ichijo|1=Ichijō family}}, and {{ill|Takatsukasa family|en|Takatsukasa family|WD=Q846799|lt=Takatsukasa|1=Takatsukasa family}} families. From then on, these five families served as ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' on a rotating basis.{{cite web|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E4%BA%94%E6%91%82%E5%AE%B6-64979|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231208093025/https://kotobank.jp/word/%E4%BA%94%E6%91%82%E5%AE%B6-64979|script-title=ja:五摂家|language=ja|publisher=kotobank|date=|archive-date=8 December 2023|access-date=12 March 2024}} {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi|1=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} was the first person in history to become a ''Kampaku'' who was not a noble by birth; his nephew {{ill|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|en|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|WD=Q967501|lt=Toyotomi Hidetsugu|1=Toyotomi Hidetsugu}} also became a ''Kampaku''. Hideyoshi obtained this title, the highest position in the aristocracy, by being adopted into the Konoe family and formally becoming an aristocrat. A retired {{transl|ja|Kampaku}} was called {{Nihongo||太閤|'''Taikō'''}}, which came to commonly refer to Toyotomi Hideyoshi.{{cite web|url=https://business.nikkei.com/atcl/opinion/16/122600033/010800002/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230905041529/https://business.nikkei.com/atcl/opinion/16/122600033/010800002/|script-title=ja:秀吉はなぜ征夷大将軍ではなく、関白を選んだか|language=ja|publisher=Nikkei Business|date=14 January 2017|archive-date=5 September 2023|access-date=29 February 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://dot.asahi.com/articles/-/202017?page=3|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240229075803/https://dot.asahi.com/articles/-/202017?page=3|script-title=ja:豊臣秀吉はなぜ「征夷大将軍」ではなく「関白」になったのか――秀吉をめぐる「三つのなぜ」|language=ja|publisher=[[The Asahi Shimbun]]|date=24 September 2023|archive-date=29 February 2024|access-date=29 February 2024}} Both {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} were styled as {{transl|ja|denka}} or {{nihongo||殿下|1=Highness|lt=Your Highness (Denka)|tenga}} in historical pronunciation; translated as "(Imperial) Highness", as were Imperial princes and princesses. ==History== In earlier times, only members of the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|en|Imperial House of Japan|WD=Q909452|lt=Imperial Family|1=Imperial House of Japan}} could be appointed {{transl|ja|sesshō}}. The {{transl|ja|[[Kojiki]]}} reports that {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ōjin|1=Emperor Ōjin}} was assisted by his mother, {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū|1=Empress Jingū}}, but it is doubtful if it is a historical fact. The first historical {{transl|ja|sesshō}} was {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|en|Prince Shōtoku|WD=Q263972|lt=Prince Shōtoku|1=Prince Shōtoku}}, who assisted {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}}. The [[Fujiwara clan]] was the primary holder of the {{transl|ja|kampaku}} and {{transl|ja|sesshō}} titles. More precisely, those titles were held by the [[:en:Hokke (Fujiwara)|Fujiwara Hokke]] (northern Fujiwara family) and its descendants, to which {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshifusa|en|Fujiwara no Yoshifusa|WD=Q960841|lt=Fujiwara no Yoshifusa|1=Fujiwara no Yoshifusa}} belonged. In 858, Fujiwara no Yoshifusa became {{transl|ja|sesshō}}. He was the first {{transl|ja|sesshō}} not to be a member of the Imperial house. In 887, {{ill|Fujiwara no Mototsune|en|Fujiwara no Mototsune|WD=Q1397196|lt=Fujiwara no Mototsune|1=Fujiwara no Mototsune}}, the nephew and adopted son of Yoshifusa, was appointed to the newly created office of {{transl|ja|kampaku}}. In the 12th century, there were {{ill|Five regent houses|en|Five regent houses|WD=Q1067142|lt=five families|1=Five regent houses}} among the descendants of Yorimichi called {{transl|ja|sekke}}: the {{ill|Konoe family|en|Konoe family|WD=Q1781840|lt=Konoe family|1=Konoe family}}, {{ill|Kujō family|en|Kujō family|WD=Q1791350|lt=Kujō family|1=Kujō family}}, {{ill|Ichijō family|en|Ichijō family|WD=Q1535498|lt=Ichijō family|1=Ichijō family}}, {{ill|Takatsukasa family|en|Takatsukasa family|WD=Q846799|lt=Takatsukasa family|1=Takatsukasa family}} and {{ill|Nijō family|en|Nijō family|WD=Q3065387|lt=Nijō family|1=Nijō family}}. Both the Konoe and Kujō families were descendants of {{ill|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|en|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|WD=Q1370620|lt=Fujiwara no Yorimichi|1=Fujiwara no Yorimichi}}, through {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadamichi|en|Fujiwara no Tadamichi|WD=Q1354407|lt=Fujiwara no Tadamichi|1=Fujiwara no Tadamichi}}. The other three families were derived from either the Konoe or Kujō families. Until the [[Meiji Restoration]] of 1868, those five families held those title exclusively with the two exceptions of {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi|1=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} and his nephew {{ill|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|en|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|WD=Q967501|lt=Toyotomi Hidetsugu|1=Toyotomi Hidetsugu}}. The offices and titles of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} were abolished by the declaration of the Imperial Restoration in 1868 during the Meiji Restoration in order to reorganize the government structure. The office and title of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} was stipulated under the former {{ill|Imperial Household Law|en|Imperial Household Law|WD=Q1324733|lt=Imperial Household Law|1=Imperial Household Law}} in 1889 and also under the new Imperial Household Law in 1948. Under these laws, the officeholder of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} is restricted to a member of the Imperial family. [[:en:Crown Prince|Crown Prince]] {{ill|Hirohito|en|Hirohito|WD=Q34479|lt=Hirohito|1=Hirohito}}, before becoming Emperor Shōwa, was {{transl|ja|sesshō}} from 1921 to 1926 for the mentally disabled {{ill|Emperor Taishō|en|Emperor Taishō|WD=Q157052|lt=Emperor Taishō|1=Emperor Taishō}}. He was called {{Nihongo3|"the Prince-Regent"|摂政宮|sesshō-no-miya}}. The area of Taikō in Nagoya is named after the title, although it refers to Toyotomi Hideyoshi. The main street is Taikō-dōri, which is served by the subway {{ill|Taiko-dori Station|en|Taiko-dori Station|WD=Q850809|lt=Taiko-dori Station|1=Taiko-dori Station}}. ==List== The following is a list of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} in the order of succession.{{cite web| url= http://nekhet.ddo.jp/ruler/japan/sekkan.html| script-title= ja:摂政・関白| access-date= 2007-09-20| language= ja| author= ネケト| location= {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=JP|1=Japan}}| url-status= dead| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20040827224301/http://nekhet.ddo.jp/ruler/japan/sekkan.html| archive-date= 2004-08-27}} The list is not exhaustive: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" |- ! scope="col" | Portrait ! scope="col" width="200px" | Name ! width="100px" | Regent title ! scope="col" width="100px"| Tenure ! scope="col" | Monarch |- |[[File:Umayado Miko.jpg|200x200px]] |'''{{ill|Prince Shōtoku|en|Prince Shōtoku|WD=Q263972|lt=Prince Shōtoku|1=Prince Shōtoku}}'''

[[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] [[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] [[ca:Sessho i Kampaku]][[de:Japanischer Regent]][[en:Sesshō and Kampaku]][[es:Sekkan]][[fa:فهرست کانپاکو و سشو در ژاپن]][[fi:Sesshō ja kanpaku]][[it:Sekkan]][[ja:摂政・関白の一覧]][[ko:섭관]][[nl:Sekkan]][[pl:Sesshō i kampaku]][[pt:Sesshō e Kanpaku]][[sh:Sesshō i kampaku]][[th:เซ็ชโชและคัมปากุ]][[vi:Sesshō và Kampaku]][[zh:攝政關白列表]] {{Short description|Types of regent in Imperial Japan}} {{About|the regent of the Emperor|the regent of a shōgun|Shikken}} {{DISPLAYTITLE:''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku''}} [[File:Japan Sessyo Flag.svg|thumb|right|250px|Imperial Standard of the Regent]] In {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}}, {{Nihongo||摂政|'''Sesshō'''}} was a {{ill|Regent|en|Regent|WD=Q477406|lt=Regent|1=Regent}} who was named to act on behalf of either a child {{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|WD=Q208233|lt=emperor|1=Emperor of Japan}} before his {{ill|coming of age|en|coming of age|WD=Q681737|lt=coming of age|1=Coming of age}}, or an {{ill|Empress of Japan|en|Empress of Japan|WD=Q595038|lt=empress regnant|1=Empress of Japan}}. The {{Nihongo||関白|'''Kampaku'''}} was theoretically a sort of chief advisor for the Emperor, but was in practice the title of both [[:en:First Minister|first secretary]] and {{ill|Regent|en|Regent|WD=Q477406|lt=Regent|1=Regent}} who assisted an adult Emperor. The duties of the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' were to convey to the Emperor the policies formulated by the {{nihongo3|[[Minister of the Left]]|左大臣|1=Minister of the Left|Sadaijin}} and other senior officials of the {{nihongo3|[[Council of State]]|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|[[Daijō-kan]]}}, and to convey the Emperor's decisions to them. As regents of the Emperor, the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' sometimes made decisions on behalf of the Emperor, but their positions were not defined by law and they had no specific political authority. The two titles were collectively known as {{Nihongo||摂関|'''sekkan'''}}, and the families that exclusively held the titles were called {{transl|ja|sekkan-ke}} ({{transl|ja|sekkan}} family). During the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}} (794–1185), from the middle of the 9th century, the [[Fujiwara clan]] began to marry off their daughters to the Emperor and assume the positions of ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', thereby excluding other clans from the political centre and increasing their political power. From the 10th century, the Fujiwara clan monopolized the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', and at the end of the 10th century, around the time of {{ill|Fujiwara no Michinaga|en|Fujiwara no Michinaga|WD=Q433133|lt=Fujiwara no Michinaga|1=Fujiwara no Michinaga}} and {{ill|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|en|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|WD=Q1370620|lt=Fujiwara no Yorimichi|1=Fujiwara no Yorimichi}}, the power of the Fujiwara clan reached its zenith. In the mid-11th century, [[:en:Emperor Go-Sanjo|Emperor Go-Sanjo]] ran his own government, and the next Emperor, {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|en|Emperor Shirakawa|WD=Q60949|lt=Shirakawa|1=Emperor Shirakawa}}, abdicated to become {{ill|Cloistered Emperor|en|Cloistered Emperor|WD=Q3053200|lt=Cloistered Emperor|1=Cloistered Emperor}}, beginning the {{ill|Cloistered rule|en|Cloistered rule|WD=Q865416|lt=Cloistered rule|1=Cloistered rule}}. From then on, the cloistered rule of Cloistered Emperor took root, and the de facto Fujiwara regime, which used the positions of ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'', was over, and the ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' lost their real political power and became mere names.{{cite web|url=https://www.juku.st/info/entry/1349|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220511095734/https://www.juku.st/info/entry/1349|script-title=ja:【藤原道長はなぜ躍進？】摂関政治をわかりやすく説明する方法|language=ja|publisher=Tomonokai|date=19 July 2015|archive-date=11 May 2022|access-date=11 March 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://news.yahoo.co.jp/expert/articles/d404674899919ce02e297e8f3a5117f8807b3341|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240312002713/https://news.yahoo.co.jp/expert/articles/d404674899919ce02e297e8f3a5117f8807b3341|script-title=ja:摂関政治で最盛期を築き上げた藤原氏とは、いかなる由緒を持つ氏族なのか|language=ja|publisher=Yahoo News|date=4 January 2024|archive-date=12 March 2024|access-date=12 March 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E6%91%82%E9%96%A2%E6%94%BF%E6%B2%BB-87197|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231129224719/https://kotobank.jp/word/%E6%91%82%E9%96%A2%E6%94%BF%E6%B2%BB-87197|script-title=ja:摂関政治|language=ja|publisher=Kotobank|date=|archive-date=29 November 2023|access-date=13 March 2024}} During the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|WD=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period|1=Kamakura period}} (1185–1333), when the warrior class seized power and the {{ill|Kamakura shogunate|en|Kamakura shogunate|WD=Q736839|lt=Kamakura shogunate|1=Kamakura shogunate}} was established, the Fujiwara were divided into {{nihongo|{{ill|Five regent houses|en|Five regent houses|WD=Q1067142|lt=Five regent houses|1=Five regent houses}}|五摂家|Go-sekke}}: the {{ill|Konoe family|en|Konoe family|WD=Q1781840|lt=Konoe|1=Konoe family}}, {{ill|Kujō family|en|Kujō family|WD=Q1791350|lt=Kujō|1=Kujō family}}, {{ill|Nijō family|en|Nijō family|WD=Q3065387|lt=Nijō|1=Nijō family}}, {{ill|Ichijō family|en|Ichijō family|WD=Q1535498|lt=Ichijo|1=Ichijō family}}, and {{ill|Takatsukasa family|en|Takatsukasa family|WD=Q846799|lt=Takatsukasa|1=Takatsukasa family}} families. From then on, these five families served as ''Sesshō'' and ''Kampaku'' on a rotating basis.{{cite web|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E4%BA%94%E6%91%82%E5%AE%B6-64979|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231208093025/https://kotobank.jp/word/%E4%BA%94%E6%91%82%E5%AE%B6-64979|script-title=ja:五摂家|language=ja|publisher=kotobank|date=|archive-date=8 December 2023|access-date=12 March 2024}} {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi|1=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} was the first person in history to become a ''Kampaku'' who was not a noble by birth; his nephew {{ill|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|en|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|WD=Q967501|lt=Toyotomi Hidetsugu|1=Toyotomi Hidetsugu}} also became a ''Kampaku''. Hideyoshi obtained this title, the highest position in the aristocracy, by being adopted into the Konoe family and formally becoming an aristocrat. A retired {{transl|ja|Kampaku}} was called {{Nihongo||太閤|'''Taikō'''}}, which came to commonly refer to Toyotomi Hideyoshi.{{cite web|url=https://business.nikkei.com/atcl/opinion/16/122600033/010800002/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230905041529/https://business.nikkei.com/atcl/opinion/16/122600033/010800002/|script-title=ja:秀吉はなぜ征夷大将軍ではなく、関白を選んだか|language=ja|publisher=Nikkei Business|date=14 January 2017|archive-date=5 September 2023|access-date=29 February 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://dot.asahi.com/articles/-/202017?page=3|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240229075803/https://dot.asahi.com/articles/-/202017?page=3|script-title=ja:豊臣秀吉はなぜ「征夷大将軍」ではなく「関白」になったのか――秀吉をめぐる「三つのなぜ」|language=ja|publisher=[[The Asahi Shimbun]]|date=24 September 2023|archive-date=29 February 2024|access-date=29 February 2024}} Both {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} were styled as {{transl|ja|denka}} or {{nihongo||殿下|1=Highness|lt=Your Highness (Denka)|tenga}} in historical pronunciation; translated as "(Imperial) Highness", as were Imperial princes and princesses. ==History== In earlier times, only members of the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|en|Imperial House of Japan|WD=Q909452|lt=Imperial Family|1=Imperial House of Japan}} could be appointed {{transl|ja|sesshō}}. The {{transl|ja|[[Kojiki]]}} reports that {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ōjin|1=Emperor Ōjin}} was assisted by his mother, {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū|1=Empress Jingū}}, but it is doubtful if it is a historical fact. The first historical {{transl|ja|sesshō}} was {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|en|Prince Shōtoku|WD=Q263972|lt=Prince Shōtoku|1=Prince Shōtoku}}, who assisted {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}}. The [[Fujiwara clan]] was the primary holder of the {{transl|ja|kampaku}} and {{transl|ja|sesshō}} titles. More precisely, those titles were held by the [[:en:Hokke (Fujiwara)|Fujiwara Hokke]] (northern Fujiwara family) and its descendants, to which {{ill|Fujiwara no Yoshifusa|en|Fujiwara no Yoshifusa|WD=Q960841|lt=Fujiwara no Yoshifusa|1=Fujiwara no Yoshifusa}} belonged. In 858, Fujiwara no Yoshifusa became {{transl|ja|sesshō}}. He was the first {{transl|ja|sesshō}} not to be a member of the Imperial house. In 887, {{ill|Fujiwara no Mototsune|en|Fujiwara no Mototsune|WD=Q1397196|lt=Fujiwara no Mototsune|1=Fujiwara no Mototsune}}, the nephew and adopted son of Yoshifusa, was appointed to the newly created office of {{transl|ja|kampaku}}. In the 12th century, there were {{ill|Five regent houses|en|Five regent houses|WD=Q1067142|lt=five families|1=Five regent houses}} among the descendants of Yorimichi called {{transl|ja|sekke}}: the {{ill|Konoe family|en|Konoe family|WD=Q1781840|lt=Konoe family|1=Konoe family}}, {{ill|Kujō family|en|Kujō family|WD=Q1791350|lt=Kujō family|1=Kujō family}}, {{ill|Ichijō family|en|Ichijō family|WD=Q1535498|lt=Ichijō family|1=Ichijō family}}, {{ill|Takatsukasa family|en|Takatsukasa family|WD=Q846799|lt=Takatsukasa family|1=Takatsukasa family}} and {{ill|Nijō family|en|Nijō family|WD=Q3065387|lt=Nijō family|1=Nijō family}}. Both the Konoe and Kujō families were descendants of {{ill|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|en|Fujiwara no Yorimichi|WD=Q1370620|lt=Fujiwara no Yorimichi|1=Fujiwara no Yorimichi}}, through {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadamichi|en|Fujiwara no Tadamichi|WD=Q1354407|lt=Fujiwara no Tadamichi|1=Fujiwara no Tadamichi}}. The other three families were derived from either the Konoe or Kujō families. Until the [[Meiji Restoration]] of 1868, those five families held those title exclusively with the two exceptions of {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi|1=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} and his nephew {{ill|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|en|Toyotomi Hidetsugu|WD=Q967501|lt=Toyotomi Hidetsugu|1=Toyotomi Hidetsugu}}. The offices and titles of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} were abolished by the declaration of the Imperial Restoration in 1868 during the Meiji Restoration in order to reorganize the government structure. The office and title of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} was stipulated under the former {{ill|Imperial Household Law|en|Imperial Household Law|WD=Q1324733|lt=Imperial Household Law|1=Imperial Household Law}} in 1889 and also under the new Imperial Household Law in 1948. Under these laws, the officeholder of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} is restricted to a member of the Imperial family. [[:en:Crown Prince|Crown Prince]] {{ill|Hirohito|en|Hirohito|WD=Q34479|lt=Hirohito|1=Hirohito}}, before becoming Emperor Shōwa, was {{transl|ja|sesshō}} from 1921 to 1926 for the mentally disabled {{ill|Emperor Taishō|en|Emperor Taishō|WD=Q157052|lt=Emperor Taishō|1=Emperor Taishō}}. He was called {{Nihongo3|"the Prince-Regent"|摂政宮|sesshō-no-miya}}. The area of Taikō in Nagoya is named after the title, although it refers to Toyotomi Hideyoshi. The main street is Taikō-dōri, which is served by the subway {{ill|Taiko-dori Station|en|Taiko-dori Station|WD=Q850809|lt=Taiko-dori Station|1=Taiko-dori Station}}. ==List== The following is a list of {{transl|ja|sesshō}} and {{transl|ja|kampaku}} in the order of succession.{{cite web| url= http://nekhet.ddo.jp/ruler/japan/sekkan.html| script-title= ja:摂政・関白| access-date= 2007-09-20| language= ja| author= ネケト| location= {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=JP|1=Japan}}| url-status= dead| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20040827224301/http://nekhet.ddo.jp/ruler/japan/sekkan.html| archive-date= 2004-08-27}} The list is not exhaustive: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" |- ! scope="col" | Portrait ! scope="col" width="200px" | Name ! width="100px" | Regent title ! scope="col" width="100px"| Tenure ! scope="col" | Monarch |- |[[File:Umayado Miko.jpg|200x200px]] |'''{{ill|Prince Shōtoku|en|Prince Shōtoku|WD=Q263972|lt=Prince Shōtoku|1=Prince Shōtoku}}'''
